draft.title: Graphs of sine, cosine and tangent
card: Sine and cosine
y = sin x and y = cos x are smooth waves between −1 and 1. The amplitude is 1 and the period is 360° (2π radians), so the pattern then repeats.
Starting points
sin x starts at 0 and rises: sin 0° = 0. cos x starts at its maximum: cos 0° = 1. The cosine graph is the sine graph shifted left by 90°.
Tangent
y = tan x has no maximum, so it has no amplitude. Its period is 180° (π radians). It has vertical asymptotes at x = 90°, 270° and so on, where cos x = 0.
Example
tan 0° = 0 and tan 45° = 1. Between the asymptotes at −90° and 90°, the graph rises through the origin and climbs without limit near each asymptote.
draft.remember: Sine and cosine repeat every 360° with amplitude 1. Tangent repeats every 180° and has asymptotes.

a.q: What is the period of y = tan x?
a.why: The tangent graph repeats every 180°, or π radians. 360° is the period of sine and cosine, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Tangent repeats twice as often as sine.

b.q: Which statement about the graph of y = tan x is correct?
opts: It has an asymptote at x = 90°
It has a maximum value of 1
b.why: At x = 90°, cos x = 0, so the graph has a vertical asymptote there. Tangent has no maximum, so it has no amplitude. The values 1 belong to sine and cosine, and tan 90° is undefined.

b.best: It has an asymptote at x = 90°

problems.detail: The example says the tangent graph 'climbs without limit near each asymptote' between −90° and 90°. Near −90° it falls without limit towards −∞; it only climbs towards +∞ near 90°. Students could picture the curve the wrong way.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer each. One card line is wrong: it says tan x 'climbs without limit near each asymptote', but near −90° the graph falls towards −∞.
